vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.2.5

The skill bundle facilitates browser data collection but exhibits high-risk behaviors and potential vulnerabilities. It explicitly instructs the AI agent to bypass the isolated browser profile in favor of the user's primary Chrome environment, exposing session cookies and personal data. The scripts `run.sh` and `collect_and_export_loop.sh` allow for arbitrary command execution via the `BRIDGE_CMD` parameter, and several scripts use `node -e` to process potentially unsanitized inputs, creating a risk of RCE. Furthermore, the skill handles sensitive credentials, such as a local admin token in `~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt` and cloud API keys, while communicating with an external endpoint (https://i-sync.cn).

llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions broadly match a browser-collection tool, but its metadata omits the environment variables and local tokens it actually reads and it will (by default) dispatch data to a cloud endpoint (https://i-sync.cn) when run in cloud mode — this mismatch and the presence of local token/file access are concerning.

dimensions.detail: The scripts and SKILL.md implement a browser-extension collection flow (local bridge or cloud dispatch) which matches the skill name/description. However the registry metadata claims no required env vars or credentials while the runtime code expects and honors several environment variables and stored preferences (WEB_COLLECTION_* vars, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, and a local admin token file). That mismatch between declared requirements and actual behavior is a red flag.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and included scripts instruct the agent to: read and write a preferences JSON under $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR or $HOME/.openclaw, read a local connector admin token from ~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt, call local bridge endpoints (e.g. http://localhost:19820/api/...), and — in cloud mode — POST wrapped payloads to a remote cloud API and poll for results. The cloud path sends a bearer token supplied by the user or preferences to https://i-sync.cn by default. These instructions directly access local files/tokens and transmit collection payloads to an external service; that behavior goes beyond a simple local helper and requires explicit user trust.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install/download step in the registry spec (instruction-only with bundled scripts). All code is included in the skill bundle; no remote archives or third-party package installs are invoked. Scripts require standard tools (curl, node) which the scripts check for at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Although the skill metadata lists no required environment variables or primary credential, the scripts consult and respect many env vars and local secrets: WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_TOKEN / WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_DEVICE_ID, WEB_COLLECTION_ADMIN_TOKEN, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_URL, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, and a local token file (~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt). The cloud mode will send a bearer token to an external domain (https://i-sync.cn). Requesting and persisting cloud tokens and reading another component's admin token file without declaring these as required credentials is disproportionate and should be disclosed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill reads and can write preference files under the OpenClaw state dir (~/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json). It may persist defaultCloudToken and other defaults. The skill is not marked always:true and does not claim to modify other skills; autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal). Users should note the skill can persist tokens/preferences locally if requested to 'apply' or 'set-key'.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key things to consider before installing or running this skill:

- Metadata mismatch: the registry says 'no required env vars', but the scripts read multiple environment variables and a local admin-token file (~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt). Treat that as a transparency/consent issue.
- Cloud dispatch: in cloud mode the skill will POST your collection payload (wrapped with device_id/action/payload) to a remote endpoint (default https://i-sync.cn) using a bearer token you supply or store. Only use cloud mode if you explicitly trust that endpoint and the token you provide.
- Local secrets: the skill will try to read an admin token file for the local bridge and will persist preferences (including possibly a cloud token) to your OpenClaw state dir. If you have sensitive tokens in those locations, either run only in local mode with care or remove/rotate tokens first.
- If you need to use it: prefer local mode (keep data in your environment), inspect scripts yourself, run the skill in a sandboxed environment first, and avoid pasting unrelated credentials. Ask the author for the upstream source/homepage and clarify why the registry metadata omitted the env/credential requirements before trusting cloud operations.
